introduction-org-charts-vs-value-streams.core: Org charts show reporting lines; value streams show how work flows to customers. Team Topologies designs teams around the flow of change, minimising handoffs and dependencies.

first_principles.problem: The org chart looks tidy, but every feature passes through five teams and waits in queues.
truths: Reporting lines don't equal work flow.

analogy.title: A factory's floor plan vs. its management chart
analogy.story: The management chart doesn't show where parts pile up waiting; the floor plan does.
analogy.breaks: Team Topologies is a model. Adapt it to your context rather than applying it dogmatically.

check.q: What does a value stream map reveal that an org chart doesn't?
check.a: Where work waits and hands off between teams on its way to customers.

the-four-fundamental-team-types.core: Team Topologies defines four team types. Stream-aligned teams own a flow of value end to end, platform teams provide self-service internal products, enabling teams coach others in new capabilities, and complicated-subsystem teams own deep-specialist components.

first_principles.problem: Ad-hoc team types ('the DevOps team', 'the integration team') create confusion and dependencies.
truths: Most teams should deliver value directly.
Shared needs are best served as products.
derivation: **Stream-aligned**: the majority; owns a product or journey.
**Platform**: reduces stream teams' load with self-service.
**Complicated-subsystem**: e.g. a video codec, a risk engine.

analogy.title: A film production
analogy.story: Directors' units (stream-aligned), studio services (platform), coaches for new techniques (enabling) and VFX specialists (complicated subsystem).
analogy.breaks: Teams can shift type over time, as when an enabling team dissolves after adoption.

steps.label: Effect
steps.detail: Clear purpose and dependencies for every team.

check.q: Which team type should make up the majority of an organisation?

minimizing-cognitive-load-the-platforms-.core: Stream-aligned teams can't also be experts in Kubernetes, networking, security and observability. The platform's job is to reduce their cognitive load with self-service, well-documented paved roads, so they focus on their domain.

first_principles.problem: Product teams spend 40% of their time on infrastructure, slowing down delivery and causing inconsistent setups.
derivation: Build a **Thinnest Viable Platform** that solves it.
Treat the **platform as a product**: measure adoption and satisfaction.

analogy.title: Utilities in a city
analogy.story: Residents don't generate their own power or treat their own water; they plug into reliable utilities.
analogy.breaks: An over-abstracted platform frustrates power users, so provide escape hatches.

example.title: Reducing load for a product team
flow: Before: own Terraform, Helm, alerts, certs

check.q: What's the platform team's primary job in Team Topologies?
check.a: To reduce stream-aligned teams' cognitive load through self-service, product-like capabilities.

interaction-modes-how-teams-talk.core: Three interaction modes. Collaboration (working closely together, temporarily, for discovery), X-as-a-Service (consuming with minimal interaction, for stable needs) and Facilitating (one team helping another learn). Choose them deliberately and evolve them over time.

first_principles.problem: Teams 'collaborate' indefinitely on everything, so dependencies and meetings explode and flow stalls.
truths: Collaboration is costly but good for discovery.
Stable interfaces should be consumed as a service.
derivation: **X-as-a-Service**: a clear API or product, low coordination.
**Facilitating**: enabling teams coach, then step back.

analogy.title: How neighbours interact
analogy.story: Building a shared fence together (collaboration), buying from the corner shop (service), or teaching a neighbour to garden (facilitating).
analogy.breaks: Mismatched expectations (one team expects a service, the other expects collaboration) create friction, so make the mode explicit.

example.title: A platform capability's lifecycle
flow: Q1: Platform + Checkout collaborate on new DB offering
Q3: Enabling team facilitates adoption by others

steps.label: Effect
steps.detail: Coordination cost drops as the capability matures.

check.q: When is the Collaboration mode most appropriate?
check.a: For time-boxed discovery of new problems, where close work speeds learning before interfaces stabilise.
